title: Deep Learning for Time Series Forecasting: Advances and Open Problems
authors: Casolaro, A.; Capone, V.; Iannuzzo, G.; Camastra, F.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of deep learning architectures for time series forecasting covering short-term and long-term models including CNNs, RNNs, GNNs, GANs, Diffusion Models, and Transformers.
problem_and_motivation: Existing reviews of deep learning for time series forecasting lack descriptions of Transformers, fail to distinguish short-term from long-term forecasting, and omit recent strategies like GNNs, Deep Gaussian Processes, GANs, and Diffusion Models. There is a need for a comprehensive survey addressing these gaps.
approach: Conducted a comprehensive literature review of deep learning methods for time series forecasting published since 2016.
Categorized architectures into short-term (CNN, TCN, RNN, GNN, Deep Gaussian Processes, GANs, Diffusion Models) and long-term (Transformer variants).
Reviewed benchmark datasets for both short-term and long-term forecasting tasks.
Analyzed advantages and limitations of each architecture class with detailed mathematical formulations.
Provided a clear distinction between models suitable for short-term versus long-term forecasting.
findings: CNNs using Euclidean kernels have limited receptive fields for capturing long-range dependencies in time series.
TCNs with dilated causal convolutions can capture long-range dependencies while maintaining computational efficiency.
RNNs suffer from vanishing and exploding gradient problems limiting long-term dependency learning.
LSTM and GRU mitigate gradient problems but still struggle with very long sequences.
GNNs can model spatial dependencies in multivariate time series through adjacency matrices.
Deep Gaussian Processes provide both predictions and confidence intervals for uncertainty estimation.
GANs can augment small datasets through synthetic time series generation or serve as end-to-end forecasting models.
Diffusion Models show promise for time series generation and forecasting tasks.

definitions.definition: Convolutional Neural Network - a deep learning architecture using convolutional layers for feature extraction.
Temporal Convolutional Network - a CNN variant using causal and dilated convolutions for sequence modeling.
Recurrent Neural Network - a neural network with recurrent connections for processing sequential data.
Long Short-Term Memory - an RNN variant with gating mechanisms to capture long-term dependencies.
Gated Recurrent Unit - a simplified LSTM variant with update and reset gates.
Graph Neural Network - a neural network operating on graph-structured data.
Deep Gaussian Process - a Bayesian model using cascaded Gaussian Processes for uncertainty estimation.
Generative Adversarial Network - a generative model with competing generator and discriminator networks.
Diffusion Model - a generative model that learns to reverse a noise diffusion process.

topics.name: Forecasting Algorithms for Sequential Spending Data
topics.justification: Comprehensive survey of deep learning forecasting architectures applicable to sequential financial data.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey provides a comprehensive taxonomy of deep learning architectures for time series forecasting, distinguishing between short-term and long-term models. It covers recent advances including GNNs, Deep Gaussian Processes, GANs, and Diffusion Models that were absent from prior reviews. The paper establishes benchmark datasets and identifies open problems for future research in time series forecasting.
directly_justifies: LSTM networks can capture long-term dependencies through gating mechanisms for sequential data modeling.
CNN-based approaches can achieve 22.6% improvement over traditional ARIMAX methods for load forecasting.
GNNs effectively model spatial dependencies in multivariate time series through graph representations.
limits: Focuses primarily on academic benchmarks rather than real-world financial applications.
Does not provide empirical comparisons across all reviewed architectures.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all topic domains. The paper directly addresses 6.B (Forecasting Algorithms for Sequential Spending Data) as its core contribution, providing a taxonomy of deep learning methods for time series prediction. Other domains were considered but rejected: 1.A-2.D (Filippino demographics not covered), 3.A-3.C (expense categorization not addressed), 4.A-4.B (personal finance systems not discussed), 5.A-5.C (financial behavioral profiles not covered), 7.A-7.E (budgeting strategies not addressed), 8.A-8.C (anomaly detection only briefly mentioned), 9.A-9.C (mobile design not covered), 10.A-10.C (privacy not discussed), 11.A-11.B (engagement not addressed), 12.A-12.C (evaluation not focused on personal finance), 13.A-13.C (savings/debt not covered), 14.A-14.C (deployment not addressed).

limitations: Does not provide empirical comparisons across all reviewed architectures on standardized benchmarks.
Focuses on general time series forecasting rather than personal finance applications specifically.
Some recent Transformer variants may not be fully covered due to rapid development in the field.
remember_this: LSTM and GRU are the most widely used recurrent architectures for time series forecasting.
CNNs with dilated convolutions can capture long-range dependencies more efficiently than standard RNNs.
GNNs enable modeling of spatial dependencies in multivariate time series data.
GANs can augment small datasets through synthetic time series generation.
Deep Gaussian Processes provide uncertainty estimates alongside predictions.
